settings.title: Q mail Accounts
settings.hint: Register your company email accounts to receive and reply from the PlanQ inbox. (Auto-sync every 5 minutes)
settings.emptyDesc: Register Gmail · Outlook · company mail or any IMAP/SMTP account
settings.confirmDeactivateDesc: Mail sync will stop but existing mail will be preserved.

settings.icloudHint: iCloud requires an "App-specific password" (Apple ID → Security)

gmail.title: Connect Gmail with an App Password
gmail.s1: First, turn on 2-Step Verification for your Google account. (App passwords require 2-Step Verification to be enabled.)
gmail.s2: Click "Create app password" below to generate a new password. Use "PlanQ" as the app name.
gmail.s3: Paste the generated 16-character password (no spaces) into the "Password" field below and save. Server settings are already filled in.

naver.title: Connect Naver Mail with an App Password
naver.s1: In Naver Mail → Settings → POP3/IMAP, turn "IMAP/SMTP" ON.
naver.s2: If you use Naver 2-Step Verification, issue an "Application password" (My Info → Security settings).
naver.s3: Enter the issued password (or your Naver login password if 2FA is off) into the "Password" field below and save.

icloud.title: Connect iCloud with an App-Specific Password
icloud.s1: Your Apple ID must have two-factor authentication enabled.
icloud.s2: Generate a new app password under "Create app password" (Sign-In and Security → App-Specific Passwords).
icloud.s3: Paste the generated app password into the "Password" field below and save.

outlook.title: Connect Outlook / Microsoft 365
outlook.s1: Turn on 2-step verification for your Microsoft account.
outlook.s2: Create an "app password" in security settings. (Regular passwords will not work)
outlook.s3: Paste the app password into the "Password" field below and save.

kakao.title: Connect Kakao Mail
kakao.s1: In Kakao Mail → Settings → IMAP/POP3, turn on "Use IMAP".
kakao.s2: Enter your Kakao account password (app password if 2-step verification is on) in the "Password" field and save.

daum.title: Connect Daum Mail
daum.s1: In Daum Mail → Preferences → IMAP/POP3, turn on "Use IMAP".
daum.s2: Enter your Daum account password in the "Password" field and save.

custom.title: Connect company or other mail
custom.s1: Ask your mail provider or company IT for the IMAP/SMTP server address and port (e.g. incoming imap.company.com:993 · outgoing smtp.company.com:587).
custom.s2: Make sure "IMAP access" is enabled in your mailbox settings (some services turn it off by default).
custom.s3: Enter the server details and your login password (or an app password if you use 2-step verification) below, then save.

rules.title: Mail sorting criteria & rules
rules.desc: Every criterion PlanQ uses to sort incoming mail is listed here. Open any criterion to see its exact conditions (the words it looks for); owners and admins can turn them on or off. Below you can add your own rules or delete learned ones. Mail itself is never deleted.

domainRule.title: Our domains
domainRule.desc: Mail sent to this domain counts as mail to us, whatever the address is. Register a domain once and you no longer need to add help@, sales@ and the rest one by one.
domainRule.note: Only register domains you own. Adding someone else's domain means bulk mail blasted at that domain also counts as "sent to us". Sending addresses are managed separately under "Sending addresses".
domainRule.errPublic: Public mail domains such as gmail.com can't be registered — the whole domain would count as ours.
domainRule.errAdmin: Only workspace admins can change this.
domainRule.appliesTo: This rule applies only to mailboxes in this workspace: {{list}}
domainRule.appliesNone: No company mailbox is connected in this workspace. Register the domain in the workspace that has the mailbox.
domainRule.removeConfirmBody: The "{{domain}}" rule will be removed. To restore it, add it again.

authDiag.title: Domain authentication (sending reputation)
authDiag.desc: For your outgoing mail to avoid spam folders, your domain needs SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. This checks live DNS right now.
authDiag.selectorPh: DKIM selector (optional — enter if you know it)
authDiag.conflict: Duplicate — receivers treat this as an error
authDiag.wildcardNote: This domain answers even for names that do not exist (wildcard DNS). So the mere existence of a name is not evidence — we judge only by record content.
authDiag.dkimWildcard: This domain answers any name you ask for (wildcard DNS), so DNS alone cannot prove whether DKIM exists. Enter the selector from your mail provider below to check that specific value.
authDiag.dkimUnknown: None of the common selectors matched. Without knowing the selector, DNS cannot prove absence — enter the selector from your mail provider below.
authDiag.spfMissing: Add the SPF record your mail provider gives you as a TXT record in your domain DNS.
authDiag.spfConflict: There is more than one SPF record. They must be merged into one — receivers treat multiple records as an error.
authDiag.dmarcMissing: Add a TXT record under _dmarc. Starting with p=none (monitor only) is the safe first step.
authDiag.lookupFailedHint: DNS did not answer. That means we could not check — not that the record is missing. Please try again shortly.
authDiag.errRate: Please try again shortly. (Per-minute lookup limit)
authDiag.note: PlanQ does not change DNS for you. Add records in the DNS management screen of wherever your domain is registered. Results are cached for 10 minutes, then re-checked.

autoExtract.recommendedDesc: Adds mail that needs a closer look, on top of reply-needed.

extraFolders.title: Import from your mail provider
extraFolders.desc: Read-only copies of your provider's Sent and Spam folders (Gmail, Naver, etc.). Nothing is moved or deleted on the provider side.
extraFolders.globalOff: Importing provider folders is paused for maintenance right now.
extraFolders.sentDesc: Mail you sent directly from your provider shows up in «Sent» and counts as a reply. The first import covers the last 30 days.
extraFolders.spamDesc: Mail your provider classified as spam appears in the «Spam» tab. The first import covers the last 14 days; items are deleted automatically 30 days after they arrive.
extraFolders.pending: The folder will be detected on the next sync
extraFolders.notFound: We couldn't find this folder in the mailbox
extraFolders.platformSender: This account sends PlanQ notifications, so its Sent folder isn't imported (to keep notices sent to other workspaces out).

spamFolder.note: Mail imported from your Gmail/Naver spam folder is deleted after 30 days. Marking it as not spam here doesn't change your provider — please also mark it as not spam in Gmail/Naver.
spamFolder.detailNote: This mail came from your provider's (Gmail/Naver) spam folder. If it isn't spam, choose «Not spam» in the ⋯ menu and also mark it as not spam in Gmail/Naver. It is deleted automatically 30 days after it arrived.

hint.all: Mail sent from PlanQ and from Gmail, other apps or AI tools
hint.other: Only mail sent outside PlanQ — Gmail, Naver web, other apps, AI tools

folder.demote: Kept out of Reply needed (auto · marketing)

folderHint.reply: Mail a person should answer. Checked from top to bottom.
folderHint.review: Nobody to reply to, but worth one look.
folderHint.demote: Bulk and automated mail with nothing to do. If a person's mail hits one of these, it goes to Worth a look instead of Reply needed.

thread_reply.title: Replies to our mail
thread_reply.desc: Someone answered a mail we sent. Fake reply headers made up by the sender's own domain are excluded.

known_contact.title: Written by someone we know
known_contact.desc: Sent directly by a client, a member, or an address we replied to before. Bulk and automated mail is filtered out first.

inbound_action.title: A new order, inquiry or reply has arrived
inbound_action.desc: Even when sent automatically, notices like “New order”, “New inquiry”, “Your inquiry has been answered” or “New ticket” go to Reply needed. Subject only. Delivery notices for things we bought, PlanQ's own notices and (광고) ads are excluded.

direct_request.title: A stranger asks us something directly
direct_request.desc: Sent straight to our address, from a personal address (personal free-mail or a two-part name at a company), with a request or a question mark. Role addresses such as info@ or help@ go to Worth a look — mark one as Reply needed twice and PlanQ learns it.

spam_rescue.title: Judged as spam, but from someone we know
spam_rescue.desc: Mail from a client, member or address we replied to that was judged as spam is lifted to Worth a look (the spam mark stays). The look of an address alone never lifts it — cold mail would come back.

security_code.title: Sign-in, verification and security notices
security_code.desc: Verification codes, new-device sign-ins, password resets, suspicious sign-ins. A code you never asked for is a sign of account takeover, so it is worth one look.

critical_notice.title: Notices you must not miss
critical_notice.desc: Failed payments, overdue bills, accounts on hold, data breaches, failed builds, booking inquiries. Subject only.

auto_ack.title: Auto-replies and receipt confirmations
auto_ack.desc: “We have received your email”, “Your inquiry has been received”, out-of-office replies. Nobody to reply to, but it confirms the other side received your mail.

schedule_notice.title: Schedule notices (booking confirmed · changed · cancelled)
schedule_notice.desc: “Your appointment is confirmed”, “Appointment date: …”, booking reminders, changes and cancellations — automated mail about something with a date on it. Nobody to reply to, but missing it means missing the appointment. Promotional wording only counts when it comes with words like confirmed/changed/cancelled or a field such as “Booking number:”.

automated_relevant.title: Automated, but about work
automated_relevant.desc: Automated mail tied to work: payments, deposits, invoices, tax invoices, receipts, reports, signatures, contracts, delivery failures, requests to finish a sign-up.

platform_notice.title: Notices sent by PlanQ
platform_notice.desc: Work notices sent by PlanQ itself. They also show inside the app — turn this off if you don't want them in the mailbox.

unclear_intent.title: From a person, but no clear request
unclear_intent.desc: Mail from a person that did not meet any Reply needed rule (including notices from role addresses). This is where such mail lands, so it can't be turned off.

ad_prefix.title: (광고) ad label
ad_prefix.desc: Mail whose subject starts with the legal Korean ad label (광고).

bulk_headers.title: Bulk-mail headers
bulk_headers.desc: Mail with unsubscribe headers (List-Unsubscribe, List-Id) or Precedence: bulk. Precedence added by auto-replies is not treated as bulk.

bulk_body.title: Unsubscribe link in the body
bulk_body.desc: Self-sent newsletters with an unsubscribe link in the body but no header.

automated_sender.title: Send-only addresses and automated mail
automated_sender.desc: noreply and notification addresses, mail-service markers (SendGrid etc.), auto-submitted markers, social notifications. Turning it off would flood Reply needed with receipts, so it can't be turned off.

transactional_notice.title: Order, delivery and payment notices for things we bought
transactional_notice.desc: Notices such as “your order”, “shipped”, “payment complete”. New orders placed with us are caught first by the “new order or inquiry” rule above.

self_sender.title: Mail we sent
self_sender.desc: Mail from our own addresses or PlanQ that came back to the inbox.

bounce.title: Bounces
bounce.desc: A mail server telling us a mail was not delivered. Shown in Worth a look.

spam_filter.title: Spam judgment
spam_filter.desc: High spam score, or put in spam by the mail provider. Mark the same domain as spam twice and PlanQ learns it.

learn.title: PlanQ learns from what you click
learn.body: Mark the same sender “No reply needed” {{d}} times and it is treated as not needing replies; move it to Reply needed {{n}} times and it always goes there; move it to Worth a look {{n}} times and it goes there. Every learned rule is listed under Mail sorting rules below and can be deleted at any time — deleting it restores the previous sorting.

criteria.ownerOnly: Only the workspace owner or admins can turn criteria on or off. Anyone can add or delete learned rules below.
criteria.saveFailed: Couldn't save. Please try again shortly.
criteria.previewFailed: Couldn't count how many mails would move. Please try again shortly.
criteria.doneNone: “{{name}}” {{state}} — no existing mail moved; it applies to new mail.
criteria.confirmBody: {{n}}{{more}} mails you already received will move ({{moves}}). You can switch it back any time, and no mail is deleted.

impersonation.title: Quarantine possible impersonation
impersonation.desc: If hidden or text-direction characters are tucked into the sender name, subject or attachment names, if the sender or link domain mixes in look-alike letters from another alphabet, or if it differs by one character from a domain you know (a client, your own company), the mail is quarantined as spam and its links are disabled. Normal single-script domains, such as Korean ones, are not flagged. Mail from someone you know is only labelled "Possible impersonation", never quarantined. Turning this off stops the quarantine but keeps the label. See the help article "How spam and impersonation mail is filtered".

learnBar.progress: Move “{{email}}” the same way once more and PlanQ will put it in {{where}} automatically from now on.
learnBar.learned: From now on, mail from “{{email}}” goes to {{where}}.

impersonation.rowHint: The sender or links show signs of imitating someone else. Open it to see why.
impersonation.noteQuarantined: Quarantined as possible impersonation. Links are disabled. If this mail is genuine, use "Not spam" in the ⋯ menu.
impersonation.noteWarn: This mail shows signs of impersonation. Check the sender before opening links or attachments.
impersonation.noteReleased: You marked this mail as not spam. The signs below are kept for reference.
impersonation.knownHint: Not quarantined because it comes from an address you know — the account may still be compromised.

signal.bidi_override: A text-direction override is hidden in the name, subject or an attachment name (e.g. a reversed company name, a file that looks like "fdp.exe").
signal.hidden_chars: Invisible characters are tucked inside words of the name, subject or an attachment name — a trick to slip past filters.
signal.mixed_script_label: The sender or link domain mixes in look-alike letters from another alphabet (Cyrillic, Greek, …).
signal.ascii_masked_label: The sender or link domain uses another alphabet to imitate an English name (e.g. "аррӏе.com").
signal.lookalike_known_domain: The domain differs by one character from a domain you know (a client, your own company).
signal.display_name_domain: The sender name contains a different company or domain than the actual sending address.
signal.reply_to_divergent: Replies are set to go to a free webmail address instead of the sending company.

trust.hint: If {{domain}} is one of your affiliate or subsidiary domains, register it as a safe domain. This warning won't appear again.
trust.confirmMessage: {{domain}} differs from {{like}} by one character. Once registered, the "one character off" warning stops for {{domain}}.
